page: Amazon Web Services r8idb.96xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors operating at clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform delivers 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs via hyperthreading at two threads per core. Memory capacity is allocated at 3072 GB, providing a ratio of 8 GB of RAM per vCPU without discrete GPU acceleration hardware.

Data throughput and persistence are supported by 22,800 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD instance storage. This substantial local flash allocation provides high-IOPS and low-latency disk access for scratch space and temporary caching. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 400 Gbps, accommodating high-throughput data ingress and egress across distributed cluster architectures.

The hardware configuration consolidates dense memory, high core counts, and high-capacity local NVMe storage into a single host footprint. These characteristics align with resource profiles required for large in-memory databases, distributed memory caches, real-time analytics engines, and enterprise transactional database environments.
description: Amazon Web Services r8idb.96xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by dedicated 3.9 GHz Intel x86_64 processors, the instance delivers 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs with two threads per core. Memory capacity reaches 3072 GB, providing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-bound applications. Local storage includes 22,800 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage, enabling high-throughput and low-latency disk operations. Network performance is anchored by a 400 Gbps baseline bandwidth configuration. The server contains no GPU hardware. By packaging extensive physical core counts, high memory density, massive local NVMe capacity, and broad network throughput into a single dedicated resource allocation, the r8idb.96xlarge is engineered for demanding workloads such as large in-memory databases, high-scale transactional systems, real-time analytics, and data-intensive enterprise processing pipelines.
